critiques.description: gap-002, gap-005, gap-017, gap-022 and gap-027 record the same unverifiable fact — that evd-001 states the sync service's placement (a virtual machine in the operations subnet, called by the kiosks over the store network) but names no firewall policy, security group, private link or mesh rule enforcing what may reach the ingest interface — and all five request substantially the same artefact. gap-009 restates it a sixth time while adding one genuinely distinct question (the fulfillment system's network location and operating party). Presented as six entries, a single silence in a ten-line note will read to a reviewer as six separate deficiencies, when one network policy document answers all of them.
critiques.rationale: Every one of the six cites only evd-001, and evd-001 contains exactly one passage bearing on reachability: 'The service runs on a virtual machine in the operations subnet. The kiosks call it over the store network.' One passage with one silence cannot yield six independent gaps; what differs between them is the threat each was raised beside, not the documentation each is about. The duplication has already produced inconsistent handling of the same fact — gap-027 rates it low severity while gap-002, gap-005, gap-017 and gap-022 rate it medium. A single gap whose related_object_ids carry all affected threats and components preserves each threat's link without multiplying the evidence request, provided gap-009's separate question about who operates the fulfillment system and where it sits survives the merge as a distinct item rather than being absorbed into the reachability question.

critiques.description: gap-001 is the gap covering what cmp-001 requires of a caller on df-001, and its requested evidence covers the authentication mechanism, any verification step in code or configuration, whether credential material is per-device or shared across kiosks, and whether repeated delivery is absorbed idempotently. It does not ask whether the service retains per-submission provenance or an ingest log. thr-001's impact leans materially on precisely that unknown — 'if per-submission provenance or an ingest log is not retained (ctx-024, unknown), injected records may not be separable from genuine ones afterwards, leaving disputed deliveries unattributable' — and map-016 deliberately routes the attribution concern away from req-LOG-002 to a catalog-gap candidate, so no object in this group asks anyone for the evidence that would settle it.
critiques.rationale: evd-001 says nothing whatever about logging: it describes receipt of order records, storage, and an hourly poll. The aggravating half of the threat's stated impact therefore rests on an unknown that no gap in this group requests an answer to, and a catalog-gap candidate against the requirement library is a note about the catalog, not a request for evidence about this system. Whether the sync service records the origin of each stored record is concrete, answerable from the same operator who would answer the authentication question, and changes the impact of thr-001 from 'fabricated orders are fulfilled and later identifiable' to 'fabricated orders are fulfilled and indistinguishable from genuine ones' — so it belongs in the evidence request that already covers the ingest path rather than being left implicit in the threat text.
